subject: VM retention & CVE closure — SOC 2 snapshot requested
messages:
From: Sam Patel <soc2-audit@brightline.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Security Reviewer <sec-contact@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: VM scan retention, SLAs, and CVE timelines for SOC 2 snapshot

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this. As part of the SOC 2 readiness review for Acme Corp we need a concise snapshot of Redwood's vulnerability management evidence for the last 12 months. Specifically: scan cadence (auth vs unauth), retention policy for full scan artifacts and incremental results, the SLA matrix you use for CVE triage/remediation by severity, and the exception/acceptance workflow (if any).

Deliverables: a short packet (PDF or ZIP) plus a CSV or spreadsheet with recent closure timestamps. If you have a one-page executive summary that would be ideal for the SOC reviewer.

Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA?

Best,
Sam Patel
Senior Auditor, BrightLine
(soc2-audit@brightline.com)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <soc2-audit@brightline.com>
Cc: ACME Security Reviewer <sec-contact@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM scan retention, SLAs, and CVE timelines for SOC 2 snapshot

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. High-level summary below; I'm attaching a compact packet and the SLA matrix.

Quick summary (executive):
- Scan cadence: nightly lightweight network scans on prod; weekly authenticated host scans; monthly full infra scans (including infra-as-code liveruns).
- Tools: commercial scanner (RapidNex) + in-house continuous runner that checks images and container manifests.
- Retention: full-scan artifacts retained 12 months (compressed offsite); incremental diffs retained 90 days; CI ephemeral scans retained 30 days. Logs for triage retained 13 months for audit purposes.
- CVE SLA (triage -> remediation): Critical: triage within 24h, mitigation/hotfix aim 72h, full remediation or documented mitigation within 7 days; High: triage 48h, remediation target 14 days; Medium: 30 days; Low: 90 days. Emergency exceptions are routed through risk-acceptance@redwood.com and documented in the exceptions repo.

Attachments: vm_scan_retention_policy_v1.pdf, cve_sla_matrix.xlsx, soc2_vulnerability_snapshot_20270607.zip

ETA: I can provide the signed one-page attestation by Friday if that's acceptable — will loop in Legal & Product Security.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Compliance — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Adding the business/attestation note for clarity: for SOC 2 we commit to the SLA windows above and to producing quarterly attestations of remediation performance (rolling 90-day snapshots). We will also provide a signed letter on company letterhead that declares our retention periods and the last 12 months of closure timestamps for Critical/High items.

I've attached a short cover letter template for auditors and the SOC checklist we use internally.

Attachment: soc2_cover_letter_template.pdf

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security & Trust — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <soc2-audit@brightline.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 13:46:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM scan retention, SLAs, and CVE timelines for SOC 2 snapshot

Technical follow-up with artifact/ops details for the packet Sam requested:
- Artifact retention: full authenticated scan buckets (prod) are stored on encrypted S3 with server-side encryption (AES256), lifecycle: 0-90d (hot), 90-365d (cold, compressed), >365d (snapshot archive subject to legal hold). Sample artifact names: prod-fullscan-YYYYMMDD-<sha>.json.
- Incremental/CI scans: stored for 30/90 days in the transient bucket, exported to archive only for triaged items linked to a ticket.
- Scan tooling & cadence: RapidNex full-run monthly; internal container-image runner triggers on PR and daily scheduled jobs for master branches.
- CVE triage process: automated priority assignment feeds into SEC-TRIAGE board; triage occurs within 24h of scanner/alert; owners are assigned; if a remediation cannot be completed in SLA the owner files an exception with risk acceptance noting compensating controls.
- Evidence export: I generated a CSV with closure timestamps for all Critical/High items in the last 12 months (attached in the ZIP). We also encrypt PII in artifact exports prior to sharing.

Related links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-TRIAGE-TEMPLATE

Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Reliability & Security
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
